title: Vishvamitra chooses the sage's light
word: the Gayatri and the peace chants
hookLine: a king puts down his crown, and the word that means worth choosing
carry: shreyas over preyas: the good is worth choosing
tomorrow: the first line never says what's worth choosing. so what is?
last: WATER FOR THE SUN, LIGHT FOR THE MIND.

cards: Line up English versions of the Gayatri and its third word comes out differently in each. Excellent. Adorable.
Worthy of worship. Most to be desired. Same Sanskrit word, a handful of tries.
Underneath all of them sits one plain idea: worth choosing. Say it slowly, and halfway through, your tongue does something it rarely does in English.

teach.h: THE N THAT CURLS THE TONGUE BACK.
teach.b: Start in the mouth. Va, easy. Then ren, but this n is different: the tongue tip curls back and touches the roof of the mouth before it lets go.
Then yam, and the lips close. Varenyam.
It means fit to be chosen, worth choosing, and it describes the radiance, not the god: like tat, it's neuter. Now go back to the king from the start of the week.
Vishvamitra had everything a person can want: an army, a throne, a kingdom. He lost one fight to a sage with a wooden staff, and then he chose.

teach.h: A KING PUTS DOWN HIS CROWN.
teach.b: In the Ramayana he puts down the crown and spends years beyond counting in austerity, to win a sage's radiance instead of a king's power. That's varenyam in a life: the light worth choosing over everything else.
The Katha Upanishad names this choice.

teach.h: SHREYAS, THE GOOD. PREYAS, THE PLEASANT.
teach.b: Two things come to every person, it says: the good and the pleasant. The wise choose the good; the foolish choose the pleasant, wanting to get and to keep. Shreyas, the good.
Preyas, the pleasant. And its verb for choose comes from the same root as varenyam.
So when Nani gets up before the kettle to say the Gayatri, here's what she's doing, as the tradition sees it: choosing, again, the light worth choosing. Worth choosing means the choice is still open.

how: Students of Sanskrit recitation practice the retroflex sounds, like the n in varenyam, with a teacher. Many Hindus say the Gayatri at dawn as a daily choice; the Katha Upanishad's teaching of the good (shreyas) over the pleasant (preyas) is often taught alongside.

games.q: what does “the gayatri and the peace chants” mean?
o: a king who gave up his crown, and the word for worth choosing
a word that means already chosen by fate
a sage who chose to become a king

games.q: the word and the choice — tap the pairs.
p: worth choosing, fit to be chosen
tongue curled back to the roof
the good: what the wise choose
the pleasant: chosen to get and keep

s: it means fit to be chosen: the choice is still open.
in the verse, varenyam describes the radiance, not Savitr
it's neuter, like tat and the radiance; Savitr is masculine.
Vishvamitra kept his throne and became a sage on the side
he gave it up to seek a sage's radiance.

games.q: Priya's cousin says getting up early to pray is pointless when you could sleep. which answer comes from the tradition?
o: praying early guarantees a better day.
the gods punish people who sleep in.
the Katha Upanishad: the wise choose the good over the pleasant, and the choice is made again each day.
games.why: shreyas over preyas. Vishvamitra chose a sage's light over a throne; Nani chooses it over a warm bed. varenyam: worth choosing.

practice: Say varenyam out loud, slowly, three times, and feel the tongue curl back on the middle n each time. Then close your mouth and sit with the quiet where the word was.
If it helps, rest a fingertip on your throat and feel the sound fade.

wordCard.voice: The Gayatri and the peace chants. Today's piece: varenyam, worth choosing, a word you feel in the mouth and a choice the tradition makes every morning.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: varenyam, worth choosing; the middle letter ण is the n said with the tongue curled back.

carryVoice: The line for today: shreyas over preyas: the good is worth choosing. Varenyam, chosen again every morning. Back tomorrow.
